study type: case-control study nested in a retrospective cohort
cohort: 251 mother-child pairs (53 cases, 198 controls) with births between 1996-2011, with cases diagnosed with ASD at the Neuropediatric Unit of the La Fe Hospital in the last 10 years
finding: The probability of ASD after birth by cesarean section is over three times that observed after unassisted vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with an increased risk of ASD (aOR = 3.36, 95% CI 1.44–7.85).
